articles.title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
When people have career or job questions, they usually tap into their network to find experts who’ve faced a similar predicament and can offer answers. Increasingly, that job is falling to AI.
SuperMe is a network of AI profiles built from the knowledge of real-life experts. When you ask a question, the platform determines which experts are best suited to answer and creates a group chat with their AI profiles.
To scale that network on both sides, meaning more users asking questions and more experts supplying knowledge, the startup announced today that it is raising $20 million in funding led by Kirsten Green at Forerunner, with participation from Greylock Partners.
Casey Winters and Ludo Antonov founded the startup in 2024. Both have experience at large consumer companies. Winters held exec roles at Grubhub, Pinterest, and Eventbrite and has advised companies like Airbnb and Canva part-time. Antonov was head of engineering at multiple startups, including Pinterest, Lyft, and Whatnot.
The two got connected when Winters was advising Whatnot. ChatGPT was becoming popular around the same time, and they decided to build a network business using AI.
“There are these hidden networks in Silicon Valley of who the best people are for niche skills. Our idea was: Could we make that network of who the absolute best people are more transparent, and could we take all of the key insights that are locked inside their heads and make them more readily available?” Winters told TechCrunch over a …

articles.title: Google leva anúncios do Modo IA a novos países; Brasil está na lista
articles.summary:
O Google anunciou a expansão dos anúncios no Modo IA da Busca para dez novos países e incluiu o Brasil entre os mercados que devem receber o recurso ainda no quarto trimestre de 2026. A iniciativa amplia a presença de publicidade nas pesquisas feitas com inteligência artificial (IA) e acompanha a mudança na forma como usuários procuram informações e produtos na internet.
Segundo Shashi Thakur, vice-presidente e gerente-geral de anúncios da Busca do Google, as consultas feitas no Modo IA são, em média, três vezes mais longas do que as pesquisas tradicionais. A empresa afirma que esse formato conversacional ajuda a compreender melhor o que as pessoas procuram e a apresentar ofertas relacionadas às suas necessidades.
Além do Brasil, o plano de expansão prevê a chegada dos anúncios à Austrália, ao Canadá, à Índia, ao Quênia, à Malásia, à Nova Zelândia, à Nigéria, ao Paquistão, às Filipinas e a Singapura. A companhia também planeja levar o recurso ao México e ao Reino Unido ainda neste trimestre.

articles.title: Wenn Werbung schützt: So nutzen Non-Profits KI als ethisches Werkzeug
articles.summary:
Wenn Werbung schützt: So nutzen Non-Profits KI als ethisches Werkzeug
Ein Kind berichtet von häuslicher Gewalt, ein Jugendlicher erzählt von seiner Flucht, ein Mädchen schildert seinen Alltag in Armut: Solche Geschichten können Menschen berühren und Spenden mobilisieren. Für Hilfsorganisationen entsteht dabei jedoch ein Dilemma: Werden die betroffenen Menschen durch Fotos, Videos oder persönliche Details erkennbar, riskieren sie Stigmatisierung, Anfeindungen oder Eingriffe in ihre Privatsphäre – möglicherweise noch Jahre nach der Kampagne. Insbesondere Kinder und Jugendliche benötigen besonderen Schutz. Werden ihre Gesichter und Lebensgeschichten öffentlich, können sie identifiziert werden. articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.summary:
Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report. This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 — July, August, and September — and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume. The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One, Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network.
Key insights
- Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%. Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year. However, variants continue to emerge, proving that IoT botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat to network infrastructure.
- Threat actors dramatically shifted their reflection and amplification tactics, abruptly abandoning CLDAP floods, which collapsed by 99.5% quarter-over-quarter. Instead, attackers pivoted heavily toward other connectionless protocols, driving a 215% surge in DNS amplification and a 122% increase in general UDP floods.
- Attack targets broadened significantly across both industries and geographies, with the United States reclaiming the most-attacked position from China. Canada and Israel experienced sharp spikes …

articles.title: 4 millions de coeurs CPU en plus : GitHub muscle son infrastructure pour faire face au code généré par IA — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Il y a quelques mois, les agents IA étaient encore un outil que les développeurs testaient avec espoir ou méfiance suivant les mentalités. Mais la situation semble avoir bien évolué : en septembre, ces outils étaient à l’origine de plus de 40 % des pull requests ouvertes sur GitHub, contre 17 % en mars.
Du moins selon les chiffres publiés par la plateforme à l’occasion d’Universe, et de son rapport annuel Octoverse, qui donnent tous deux la mesure du phénomène. Sur les douze mois achevés fin septembre, les développeurs ont poussé du code 17,9 milliards de fois, plus qu’en 2024 et 2025 réunis, détaille GitHub sur son blog.
Les commits, ces instantanés de modifications, ont atteint le nombre de 34,3 milliards, contre 12,9 milliards un an plus tôt. La courbe s’est surtout cabrée à partir de juin : en septembre, GitHub enregistrait environ six fois plus de commits qu’en septembre 2025. Une montée en charge qu’on a d’ailleurs pu observer (ou subir) cet été avec les « quelques » ralentissements de la plateforme.
Quatre millions de cœurs CPU de plus, et ça ne suffira pas
Pour suivre la cadence, GitHub a ajouté depuis janvier 4 millions de cœurs CPU à son infrastructure, 160 pétaoctets de stockage haute vitesse et 50 Tb/s de capacité réseau. Mais le volume de code n’est ici qu’une partie du problème : chaque commit ou pull request déclenche en effet une cascade de tâches automatisées (tests, vérifications de style, analyses de sécurité). articles.title: Risco de colapso de correntes do Atlântico é ignorado em planos climáticos; Brasil é exceção
articles.summary:
Um sistema de correntes oceânicas essencial para regular o clima da Terra pode sofrer um enfraquecimento significativo até o fim do século, mas o risco ainda é ignorado pela maioria dos governos em seus planos de adaptação climática. De 91 planos nacionais apresentados à Convenção das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima, apenas dois mencionam a possibilidade de colapso dessas correntes — e nenhum deles prevê medidas concretas para enfrentar o cenário.
O alerta foi publicado em artigo na revista Nature Sustainability, elaborado por pesquisadores que analisaram como os países se preparam para possíveis mudanças na circulação do Oceano Atlântico.
O sistema em questão é a Circulação Meridional de Revolvimento do Atlântico, conhecida pela sigla AMOC. Ela funciona como uma espécie de esteira transportadora oceânica: leva águas quentes da superfície em direção ao norte do Atlântico e devolve águas mais frias para o sul em camadas profundas.
Esse movimento redistribui calor pelo planeta e influencia temperaturas e padrões de chuva em regiões muito distantes do oceano. Com o aquecimento global, a circulação está enfraquecendo e pode continuar a perder força ao longo deste século.
Os pesquisadores ressaltam, porém, que um colapso completo é considerado improvável antes de 2100. Um estudo recente citado pelos autores projetou redução de 50% na intensidade da AMOC até o fim do século em cenário intermediário de emissões.

articles.title: Why Physics Needs To Move At The Pace Of Design
articles.summary:
Physics-based analysis becomes more consequential as chips, packages, boards, and systems are designed together.
Every hardware design contains decisions made before the team fully understands their physical consequences. An architecture is chosen. Components are placed. Materials are selected. Engineers bring experience and judgment to those choices, but the detailed physics often arrives later, when changing course is harder and more expensive.
That order of work limits what engineers can build. When every answer requires substantial preparation, compute and specialist time, teams have to decide which questions are worth asking. Promising ideas can be set aside because there is no practical way to investigate them within the schedule.
We built Vinci to change that. We recently announced a $250 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation. The investment gives us the resources to accelerate a goal that reaches well beyond any single analysis: shortening the distance between what engineers can imagine and what they can build.
The cost of slow analysis extends into decisions made long before a simulation begins. Teams simplify designs so they can evaluate them. They add margin where uncertainty remains. They carry assumptions forward because testing every alternative would take too long.

articles.title: Why Africa needs its own AI off switch
articles.summary:
Imagine that it is 6 a.m. in the wholesale markets of Nairobi. Merchants are delivering vegetables from up-country farms to the retailers who sell to the city’s households. Everyone is using M-Pesa, Safaricom’s mobile money platform, when suddenly, the system crashes, bringing the market to a standstill. Imagine that across the continent in Accra, MTN’s MoMo has also crashed, and business in Makola Market has all but stopped.
With the growing number of cyberattacks caused by artificial intelligence, these are highly plausible scenarios. In both these cases, Safaricom, MTN, and the Kenyan and Ghanaian governments need an off switch, or the technical ability and know-how to stop a rogue AI agent from executing its code on their payment systems.
Currently, the conversation on AI agents revolves around China versus the U.S., open versus closed models, and who will dominate the AI race. But in Africa’s capitals, the distinction that will ultimately matter is not whose product was used to build a system, or who dominates whom, but rather whether AI can serve its purpose and be controlled locally. So how can Africa build with agency, and with control over the code and makeup of its own systems, even though they are built on foreign technology?

articles.title: Safaricom fires 118 staff for fraud even as incidents fall 82%
articles.summary:
Safaricom dismissed 118 employees for fraud in the year to March, even as fraud incidents fell 82%, pointing to a declining insider threat amid an intensified crackdown at Kenya’s largest telecoms operator.
The figure, disclosed in the company’s 2026 Sustainable Business Report released on Tuesday at its Nairobi headquarters, is more than four times the 28 dismissals recorded in the year to March 2021. It equates to about 2% of the 5,648 people the report lists as employees.
Earlier disclosures put the tally at 95 in the year to March 2024 and 113 in the year to March 2025, so the climb has been steady rather than a one-off spike.
Insider conduct carries unusual weight at Safaricom as staff sit close to customer data, SIM registration and the agent network that moves money across M-PESA, Kenya’s dominant mobile-money platform. The report treats theft, falsifying company records, and unauthorised access to customer call records as gross misconduct that can result in dismissal.
“Our customers entrust us with their personal information, communications and financial transactions and expect our services to be secure, reliable and responsible,” Safaricom said in the report.
The report lists 118 fraud cases investigated and 118 dismissals, along with three disciplinary warnings, up from none the prior year. Referrals to law enforcement doubled from seven to 14. Fraud was the most common concern raised through Safaricom’s anonymous ethics hotline.

articles.summary:
El Nokia 1100, considerado el teléfono móvil más vendido de la historia, puede encontrarse hoy desde USD 70 en plataformas de segunda mano como eBay. Más de 20 años después de su lanzamiento, el modelo sigue despertando interés por una combinación que marcó su época: bajo coste, resistencia y funciones básicas que resolvían una necesidad concreta.
El dispositivo llegó al mercado en 2003 con un precio cercano a USD 100. Su éxito se relacionó con la posibilidad de acceder a llamadas y mensajes sin depender de cámaras, conexión a internet o pantallas a color. En 2026, conseguir una unidad nueva resulta casi imposible, pero el interés por los teléfonos clásicos mantiene activos los anuncios de ejemplares usados.
El Nokia 1100 superó los 250 millones de unidades vendidas
El alcance comercial del Nokia 1100 no ha sido superado por otro celular. Según datos de Visual Capitalist, basados en informes de Yahoo Finance y Omdia, el modelo vendió más de 250 millones de unidades en todo el mundo.
El segundo puesto también pertenece a Nokia. El Nokia 1110 alcanzó 248 millones de equipos vendidos, mientras que el iPhone 6 y el iPhone 6 Plus sumaron 222 millones de unidades. La distancia ilustra el impacto que tuvo el modelo lanzado en 2003.

articles.title: Unlocking Tensor Core Performance for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Atomistic simulations help researchers understand how molecules and materials behave, from chemical reactions and phase transitions to mechanical failure. These simulations come with a cost-accuracy trade-off. Quantum-mechanical methods such as density functional theory (DFT) can provide accurate energies and forces, but their computational cost often limits their use for large systems or long simulations. Classical interatomic potentials are much faster, but their fixed functional forms limit accuracy and generalizability across different atomic environments. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) help bridge this gap. They use neural networks to predict potential energies and interatomic forces at a fraction of the cost, enabling researchers to study larger systems and longer timescales while retaining much of the required accuracy.
Running an MLIP efficiently, however, presents its own challenge. Atomistic simulations are sensitive to small errors that can accumulate over time and are most visible when computing forces, which are obtained by differentiating the predicted energy. During molecular dynamics simulations, these forces guide updates to atomic velocities and positions over many timesteps, making numerical precision important not only for physical accuracy but also for the stability of the resulting trajectory.

Cisco on Wednesday released fixes for an exploited vulnerability affecting its Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) software.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76418 and assigned a CVSS score of 8.6, the bug resides in the Remote Access SSL VPN service. Attackers can exploit it remotely, without authenticating, to force the device to restart unexpectedly and disrupt its availability.
Cisco attributes the issue to logic errors affecting tunnel groups configured with secondary authentication. Exploitation involves a malicious request sent while connecting to the SSL VPN.
“A successful VPN login is not required to reach the affected processing path,” Cisco noted.
For an attack to work, the firewall must be running an unpatched release, have its SSL VPN login service reachable, and use secondary authentication in an affected tunnel group. The company’s cloud-delivered firewall and management offerings, Secure Access, and the Secure Firewall Management Center are not vulnerable.
Cisco’s product security team learned in October that the flaw was being exploited in the wild. No information has been shared about the attacks or the threat actors behind them.
The vulnerability came to light during a Cisco TAC support case, and the company credited Eric Fernald with finding it.

The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. But as an image-accuracy enthusiast, trained calibrator, and resident display expert, what excites me most about the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the technology it uses to display an accurate picture. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. It could be the future for displays.
Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination). For nearly a century, CIE 1931 has been a reliable calibration target, and most of the reference modes on the new MacBook use it.
But with the development of new display technologies over the past 20 years that have ultra-narrow band spectra — such as OLED, LEDs with KSF phosphors, and quantum dots — CIE 1931’s shortcomings are increasingly apparent. Even when calibrated to the same D65 white point, the same image on an OLED and quantum dot LED can look identical to one person, but different to another because of biological variations in our eyes. “There isn’t a challenge in creativity, and there isn’t a challenge in talent. articles.title: Cómo eliminar un virus troyano que se haya instalado en el computador
articles.summary:
Un computador que empieza a fallar sin motivo aparente, con ventanas que se abren solas o un tráfico de internet que se dispara, puede estar albergando un troyano. Este tipo de malware se cuela disfrazado de programa inofensivo y, una vez dentro, puede operar sin que el usuario lo note.
Un troyano es un software malicioso que se presenta como un programa legítimo para infiltrarse en un sistema. Permite robar credenciales, cookies, archivos y datos bancarios, e incluso secuestrar el equipo para ataques de denegación de servicio (DDoS), sin que la víctima perciba su presencia.
Cómo llega un virus troyano al computador
Los troyanos no se instalan solos, necesitan que el usuario los ejecute sin saberlo. Los sitios web de archivos compartidos, entre ellos los de torrents, son una fuente habitual, ya que un atacante puede subir un software pirateado con el virus oculto dentro.
Los archivos adjuntos de correo electrónico también son una puerta de entrada frecuente. Pueden llegar en mensajes genéricos o dirigidos a un grupo específico de personas, con un documento que simula ser inofensivo.
A esto se suman los mensajes falsos en aplicaciones de chat, con nombres de usuario casi idénticos a contactos reales, los sitios web infectados que redirigen las descargas a servidores maliciosos, y las redes WiFi pirateadas, que imitan una red legítima para enviar al usuario a páginas falsas.

articles.summary:
Separate false failures caused by voltage droop from real structural defects.
By Aakash Jani, Henrique Mendes, and Robert Wilcox
In a previous blog, we highlighted the importance of combining physical and functional sensors to plan for new workloads. This use case remains relevant for high-performance AI and HPC systems because ‘spiky’ workloads induce severe droops that dominate power budgets.
Your $1 billion ASIC just had a scan failure during an In-System Test. How can you tell whether the failure is an actual structural failure, or one caused by physical phenomena like voltage droop? Scan patterns can often generate intense switching activity when long or multiple chains are toggled, which may induce a voltage droop. If the failure is due to a voltage droop, you have a few options: slow the shift clock, raise the voltage, or repartition your scan patterns. Without physical sensors that report conditions during the test, teams can’t tell the two cases apart and might throw away good parts on false failures.
Co-mingling physical and functional sensors is necessary across the system lifecycle because functional and physical failures are connected. Let’s move further down the system lifecycle into silicon deployment for another example.

articles.summary:
French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month.
The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: Hackers Steal 2.6 Million Records From Sony’s Japanese ISP So-net
articles.summary:
Hackers have stolen the personal information of current and former So-net and Plala internet subscribers in Japan, Sony Network Communications announced on October 27. Nearly 2.6 million records were impacted.
The attackers broke into the So-net member database on October 19. The company first spotted the intrusion on October 23, then took the targeted server offline and cut off traffic coming from the attackers.
By the following day, its investigators had confirmed that personal data had been taken and determined the scope of the leak.
The stolen information includes names, dates of birth, gender, phone numbers, email addresses, user IDs, and the IDs customers use to connect to the internet.
Of the roughly 2.6 million exposed records, 2.14 million belong to So-net subscribers and 443,000 to Plala (S Course) subscribers. Roughly 293,000 of them relate to people who left the services in March 2026 or later, as their details are kept for some time to handle final bills and support requests.
The hackers also obtained approximately 54,000 email addresses, along with their passwords, belonging to four additional mail services: Mail Service (G), A-Box, So-net VAIO Mail, and the PostPet email account service. So-net has not identified any password leak for the free basic mailbox that comes with a subscription.
On October 27, the company began resetting the passwords for the impacted email addresses, forcing users to set new ones before they could resume using the services.

articles.title: The 5 essential layers of AI agent sandboxing on Kubernetes

The 5 essential layers of AI agent sandboxing on Kubernetes
An AI agent given autonomy to run code will inevitably run code no human has reviewed. It may install model-selected packages, run scripts generated moments earlier, and iterate until a developer’s test passes; that risk is limited to a laptop. For a company, it can extend beyond the agent’s workload to any workload deployed on shared Kubernetes infrastructure. Cluster configurations can limit a container’s system calls, but an allowed call that reaches a kernel vulnerability can still expose the underlying node.
As agents proliferate, this gap has shifted workload isolation from a niche hardening requirement to a baseline need for platforms that run agents. This is a challenge our users at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) have asked us to help solve.

As expected in the cloud-native space, the community has developed solutions. These solutions exist across five layers: from the pod request, down to the node, and back up to the agent’s session. Platform teams can assemble the stack rather than reinvent it, while native provider support simplifies configuration and maintenance. Managed Kubernetes services offer sandboxed pods this way, but runtimes isolate agentic workloads differently.

articles.title: Physics-Based Validation: The Foundation Of Trustworthy Agentic EDA
articles.summary:
What self-verifying agents validate their decisions against and why physics-based engines are the authority on correctness.
This is the third article in a series examining what it takes to build production-ready AI agents for EDA. The first explored the architectural decisions required for agents to operate reliably in production environments. The second examined what self-verifying means in an agentic EDA workflow: how agents continuously check their decisions as they work, rather than waiting until the end of a run.
But what exactly are those decisions being verified against?
The answer is physics. More specifically, the deterministic, physics-based EDA engines that define whether a design is correct. A self-verifying agent checks its own work, and a physics-validated workflow confirms that work is correct.
Chip design has always faced physics-based constraints. Every transistor, every wire, every timing path, and every thermal gradient is governed by the fixed laws of physics, regardless of how the design was created. This is why tapeout is binary: silicon either works or it does not.
When AI enters this domain, that physical reality does not change. The relevant question is not whether an AI system can reason about physics, but whether the outputs it produces have been confirmed by the engines that enforce that physics.
That distinction separates a model that is capable of reasoning about physics from a workflow that is physics-validated.

articles.title: Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
articles.summary:
Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
Ask a platform team what they built last year, and the list likely includes a Kubernetes controller that creates a few objects in order and copies fields between them. No business logic, just wiring. A Deployment, a Service in front of it, and a ConfigMap whose one interesting value is the hostname the Service reports in its status. Kubebuilder turns building the first controller into a pleasant afternoon. The tenth brings its own reconcile bugs, upgrade path, and on-call rotation. It’s the same controller. It’s slightly different each time, and it exists in thousands of organizations.
Every ingredient, no recipe
Kubernetes has the ingredients: CRDs define new types. Controllers give them behavior. Server-side apply tracks who owns each field. CEL evaluates expressions, and OpenAPI schemas type every field. What Kubernetes does not provide is the recipe. Nothing says that several resources form one thing, or that a value in one comes from the status of another and must wait for it.

The challenge is making hundreds of private APIs safely reachable by agents without exposing them to the public internet, without giving models control over identity, and without flooding context windows with hundreds of tool definitions.
MoEngage, the agentic customer engagement platform that more than 1,350 consumer brands use to deliver personalized experiences across push, email, in-app, SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS, faced exactly this problem. Behind the product sit roughly 400 internal REST APIs, built by 25 engineering teams, running in private virtual private clouds (VPCs) across seven AWS Regions. MoEngage isolates these APIs regionally to meet data residency commitments and doesn’t expose them to the public internet. The capability the agents needed was already running in production. Making it reachable, safely, was the hard part.

articles.title: Is It Getting Hot In Here? Why Thermal Is No Longer A Signoff Problem
articles.summary:
Applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process is key to effective thermal analysis.
AI, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging have pushed power density higher, and that means managing heat is becoming one of the most consequential challenges in electronic design.
The issue is no longer simply how to cool a chip after it has been designed. Thermal behavior now affects decisions spanning device performance, package architecture, mechanical stress, reliability, floor planning and ultimately system performance. So engineering teams must shift thermal analysis to earlier in the design process as they consider a much broader multi-physics strategy.
Traditionally, engineers could isolate and analyze many physical effects separately. Electrical performance could be evaluated in one environment, thermal behavior in another and mechanical stress in another and so on. But with increasing integration, a change intended to improve performance in one domain can create unintended consequences elsewhere. Higher power can increase temperature; temperature can change electrical behavior; and thermal expansion can introduce mechanical stress that ultimately affects reliability.

Gallup began tracking employee engagement in 2000, when 26% of employees in the US said they were engaged. That figure stayed steady between 26% and 30% through 2013, then climbed to a peak of 36% in 2020.
But engagement has fallen since the start of the decade. It stood at 29% last quarter, the lowest level in 15 years. It's also two percentage points lower than the previous quarter.
Gallup writes that each percentage point in engagement represents approximately 1.6 million US employees. The Q3 decline is equivalent to about 3.2 million fewer engaged workers, bringing the total decrease since 2020 to approximately 11 million.
The decline reflected two aspects of employees' work experience: knowing what is expected of them and feeling cared about as a person.
Gallup says businesses should care more about their employees' morale, as disengaged workers can impact a firm's productivity, customer service, quality, safety and profitability.

Reservar un nombre casi idéntico al de una persona, una marca o una institución es más sencillo de lo que parece, y la propia compañía reconoce el problema al bloquear de antemano ciertos nombres.

El proceso se activa desde Ajustes > Cuenta > Nombre de usuario, admite solo letras minúsculas, números, puntos y guiones bajos, y requiere al menos una letra. Como cada nombre es único, la aplicación ofrece un generador de sugerencias para cuando la opción deseada ya está tomada.

articles.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
articles.summary:
Which AI agents can act inside your employees' browsers today? If an agent started browsing this morning, would you know it wasn't the employee? Most security teams can't answer those questions yet. That's not a failure of effort. It's a sign of how quickly AI moved from answering questions to taking action.
AI agents now operate browsers inside authenticated applications, and they get there in different ways: debugging interfaces, extensions, agentic browsers, and emerging standards like WebMCP. Each changes what an agent can access, how its actions are attributed, and whether existing controls can see them.
1. Remote Debugging: Applications Controlling the Browser
One way AI agents operate browsers isn't new at all. It's the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
CDP was built to help developers inspect, debug, and automate Chromium-based browsers. It provides programmatic access to navigation, page content, network activity, and user interactions. Tools like Playwright and Puppeteer have used it for years. AI agents use the same approach to navigate websites, extract information, fill forms, and interact with web applications.
The key distinction: automation doesn't have to originate inside the browser. An external application can connect to a browser with debugging enabled and control its tabs. If that browser has authenticated sessions, the automation can use that access.

Artificial Intelligence
Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro
When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling. A PHP codebase built over the years with Laravel, Symfony, or Doctrine carries business rules in places that are not obvious, from Eloquent traits to XML mapping files, so a structurally similar Java port can compile cleanly and still behave differently.
This post shows how to turn PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process using Kiro. Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi-step engineering tasks with you in the loop. The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight-phase workflow. This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.

- Familiarity with PHP (Laravel/Eloquent or Symfony/Doctrine). Java knowledge (Spring Boot, JPA) helps you review the generated output, but the engine produces idiomatic Java for you, so you don’t need to rewrite the application in Java yourself.

articles.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot

Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
A powerful feedback loop could drive more warming than predicted.
Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.
Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century.

Application teams should spend more time building software and less time assembling infrastructure. But for organizations in regulated industries, getting an application running is only the beginning.
A patient scheduling system, financial application, government service, or aerospace workload may remain in production for years. During that time, operating systems need patching. Runtimes reach end of support. Security requirements evolve. Applications scale. Teams change. Auditors ask for evidence. Regulatory frameworks expand.
For these organizations, the question is no longer simply: How quickly can we deploy? It is: How easily can we deploy, and keep that application secure, supported, observable, auditable, and operational for years?
“The services built for fast starts also need to support long stays.”

Quand Mistral a présenté son tout nouveau modèle d’intelligence artificielle Mistral Large 4, alias Le Chonk, le 6 octobre, la start-up française n’avait mis en place qu’un accès payant par API. Elle avait cependant promis d’ouvrir les poids du modèle à la fin du mois. Chose promise, chose due. Trois semaines plus tard, les fichiers sont en ligne.
Depuis ce jeudi 29 octobre, ces poids ouverts sont à retrouver sur le site Hugging Face, comme Mistral l’annonce sur son blog et sur X.
Dans un modèle d’IA, les poids sont la myriade de réglages appris durant la phase d’entraînement. Les télécharger permet de faire tourner le modèle sur ses propres serveurs, sans envoyer ses données chez Mistral. Sur le papier, le modèle s’appuie sur 1 000 milliards de paramètres. Mais dans les faits, il n’en mobilise que 49 milliards par token (un fragment de mot), 52 milliards si l’on compte les couches d’entrée et de sortie.
Ce tri est voulu. Mistral Large 4 repose sur une architecture appelée MoE, pour mélange d’experts (Mixture of Experts). Dans les grandes lignes, le modèle est découpé en 128 « experts » spécialisés, et seuls quatre d’entre eux (plus un expert commun) entrent en jeu pour chaque token. À titre de comparaison, son prédécesseur Mistral Large 3 a 675 milliards de paramètres, dont 41 milliards utilisés par token (même approche MoE).
Qu’est-ce qui a changé pour Mistral Large 4 ?

For more than two decades, the standard playbook for Australian businesses online was straightforward: identify target keywords, optimize metadata, acquire authoritative backlinks, and compete for a spot in Google’s “ten blue links.”
That paradigm has fundamentally fractured.
With the rollout of Google AI Overviews and the rise of conversational answer engines like ChatGPT Search and Perplexity, search engines are shifting from navigational directories to synthesis engines. Instead of presenting users with a list of external destinations to evaluate, large language models (LLMs) parse the web in real time, extract key facts, and deliver direct, conversational answers.
For digital marketers and business leaders across Australia, this shift presents a new challenge: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO). To remain visible, brands must learn how to earn recommendations and citations directly inside AI-synthesized answers.
What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is the practice of structuring, writing, and technically delivering website content so that it can be accurately crawled, ingested, and cited by generative AI engines.
While traditional SEO focuses on maximizing organic rank positions and direct page clicks, GEO focuses on information gain and citation share. It’s structuring and adding information to a webpage that improves the chances that an AI agent selects your brand (or page) as a primary source when answering user queries.

Demand for more powerful AI chips is pushing semiconductor design forward, but commercializing those designs depends on whether chip manufacturing and packaging technologies can keep up.
A far less visible part of the semiconductor ecosystem is therefore coming into focus: the equipment, components, and materials used to manufacture and package advanced chips. As semiconductor processes become more precise and performance requirements rise, materials must operate reliably under more demanding conditions. Materials engineering helps bridge the gap between advanced chip designs and what manufacturers can produce reliably at scale.

Semiconductor manufacturing already requires materials that perform in highly specialized environments. Components used in semiconductor processing equipment must withstand extreme operating conditions, resist mechanical wear, and maintain process stability and precision.

Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.
AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. But these rules assume that companies can see what their agents are doing and why—when in reality, they lack sufficient visibility.

Detecting an AI agent attack isn’t simply finding multiple small needles scattered in a large haystack; it is recognizing whether and for what purpose the needles are connected.
Traditional security controls evaluate single actions to classify whether an intent is bad or benign. This approach fails on AI agent activity when the bad intent only emerges over a series of benign actions. It only becomes apparent if and when the overall sequence of actions is viewed or actioned.
Fraud detection is an example. A bank analyzes each purchase on its own. That’s largely how traditional security operates. Fraud detection, however, needs to see patterns of apparently benign single purchases across multiple purchases, possibly in multiple locations with unlikely timing (potentially employing agent capability). “Agent security needs the same combination of pattern detection and evidence, applied to the steps an agent takes rather than to purchases,” writes Cisco in announcing the open sourcing of its Project Quarry.
Cisco describes Quarry as a neurosymbolic rule language, combining machine learning judgment with rule-based checks. “It covers single-turn and multi-turn large language model (LLM) conversations, agents, tool use, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions, and multimodal inputs.”

El máximo responsable de la red social de Meta sostuvo en el podcast Colin y Samir que la percepción ya se deteriora en las plataformas de Meta y que la tendencia continuará durante los próximos años.

Mosseri afirmó que las inquietudes de los usuarios abarcan la propiedad de sus contenidos, el entrenamiento de modelos de IA con ese material, la seguridad de los datos personales y el posible reemplazo de puestos de trabajo. Sobre esa premisa han seguido tres lustros de MacBook sin pantalla táctil.
Este miércoles, John Ternus ha presentado un MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil.
Lo fácil es leerlo como una enmienda a Jobs, como un tabula rasa respecto a la larguísima sombra del fundador. Pero lo interesante es cómo justifica Ternus el cambio, porque ahí aparece el criterio con el que va a dirigir la empresa, presumiblemente.
En 2021, siendo jefe de ingeniería de hardware, Ternus le dijo a la enorme Joanna Stern que el Mac estaba optimizado para la entrada indirecta y que no veían motivos para cambiarlo. Cinco años después, en su entrevista con Steven Levy en Wired, arranca con la misma idea: el Mac es, ante todo, un dispositivo de entrada indirecta.
El principio es el mismo. La conclusión, la contraria. Lo que ha cambiado lo explica él mismo: necesitaban llegar a un punto en que el tacto no empeorase el producto en nada, ni en peso ni en grosor. SecurityScorecard benchmark tests AI on third-party risk work and resistance to attack
Security ratings company SecurityScorecard Inc. today released an open benchmark for testing whether artificial intelligence models can handle third-party risk management work without being turned against the companies using them.
The TPRM Benchmark is built for vendor risk programs, where a model may need to interpret security telemetry and decide which exposures matter. A lot of what the model reads comes from questionnaires and documents that vendors filled out themselves, and parts of that may be incomplete or manipulated on purpose. SecurityScorecard says generic benchmarks built around static or academic tasks were not designed with that in mind.
On the capability side, tasks cover disciplines such as exposure triage and fourth-party technology risk, and each one starts as a snapshot of SecurityScorecard’s own vendor-risk telemetry that domain experts check before any model is scored. Scores are measured against a baseline with confidence intervals attached, and each model gets an autonomy readiness level from L0 to L4 based on its performance across repeated trials. SecurityScorecard says the rating is meant to show how far a model can be trusted to work without human oversight.

articles.title: Auto-Generation Of Properties: Methodology Insertion

Technology is only useful if it improves an existing methodology. Property generation is still refining that goal, but in the long term it could be very useful.
Key Takeaways:
A top-down semiconductor development flow has long been a goal for chip design, and shift left is certainly making that increasingly possible. The problem is that the starting point — the specification — is often incomplete or nonexistent, because the chip industry has been notoriously bad at writing specifications.
There are several ways to insert AI into existing flows. But just because something can be done doesn’t mean it should be. This is one of the big challenges facing AI adoption. Many existing tasks could be done more efficiently using an agentic flow, but it’s not clear whether that is the right thing to do.
This limitation becomes especially apparent when AI starts to help with something that has been woefully inadequate in the past — the creation of good, complete specifications. The big question is whether AI can enable designs, or verification environments, to be automatically derived from a specification. Perhaps a more correct goal is whether AI can help create better specifications. With better specifications, downstream design becomes a lot easier.

articles.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience | TechCrunch

Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”

articles.summary:
Why MCP servers should tell agents what to do next
Many MCP servers do one thing. An agent asks for data, and the server hands it back. AWS’s James Ward thinks that leaves a lot on the table. The protocol works best, he told me, when the server acts less like a database and more like another voice in the conversation.
Ward is a principal developer advocate at AWS and sits on the technical committee of the Agentic AI Foundation, the Linux Foundation group that now houses MCP. I sat down with him last week at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose the day before he and co-presenter Alexander Ioffe were set to give a session on moving MCP from a basic API to an agent integration interface.
“Many times our MCP servers are just these APIs, like ‘get me the customers,’ and that is a good place to start,” Ward said. “I imagine MCP as the third person in this conversation, or a fourth or a fifth, depending on how many MCP servers you have.”
In practice, that means a tool response carries guidance with the data. It tells the agent what it just did, what it might want to do next, and where to find more.
The other half of his pitch is visibility. Web developers can trace a click on a page all the way down to the database. “MCP by default doesn’t have any way to do trace ID,” Ward said.

That passage dominated the Hacker News discussion, where commenter jonahx set out what it trades away:
There is no longer anyone to turn to if this system breaks by, eg, having a critical bug that no one can figure out. No causal model in anyone’s head that can be appealed to, to slowly and methodically debug. The new trust model is: We trust Claude to always understand the system enough to debug anything or make any reasonable change we could want.

Discover seven things emotionally intelligent people do differently to manage emotions, communicate better, and build healthier relationships.
Emotional intelligence is not about staying calm all the time or knowing exactly what to say in every situation. It is about understanding your emotions, recognising how others feel, and choosing how to respond rather than reacting impulsively.
In everyday life, emotional intelligence can influence how we handle disagreements, build relationships, respond to criticism, and navigate difficult situations. People who develop this skill are often better equipped to communicate clearly, understand different perspectives, and manage their emotions constructively.
The good news is that emotional intelligence is not simply something you are born with. Many of its essential skills can be practised and strengthened over time.
7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
1. They pause before reacting
When someone criticises them, disagrees with them, or says something hurtful, emotionally intelligent people try not to respond immediately out of anger.
They understand that an emotional reaction can sometimes make a difficult situation worse. Instead of sending an impulsive message or saying something they might regret, they give themselves time to process what happened.

Cloudflare ties the drop, tentatively, to law enforcement action earlier this year against four of the largest botnets built from compromised internet of things devices.
The Justice Department announced the disruption of Aisuru, Kimwolf, JackSkid and Mossad in March, when authorities in Canada and Germany also moved against people allegedly behind them. Internet of things botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat in Cloudflare’s assessment, with new variants such as Dysphoria and Evooo1Bot already circulating.
August was the heaviest month for Mirai-classified traffic, at 57.23 petabytes. The quarter’s longest Mirai attack began Aug. 19 and kept going for 49.7 hours.

The new model does ship with the latest firmware, though. It also works with a regular USB mouse now. GEOS shipped with the original 64C back in 1986, too, so the pairing doubles as a neat nod to the machine's past.

articles.title: When Risk Becomes Personal: What Security Leaders Can Learn From a Cancer Diagnosis
articles.summary:
Risk management leaders educate people on measuring exposure, testing assumptions and advising on how best to prepare for incidents they hope won’t occur. They know that the absence of a security alert does not stand for safety; that resilience depends on preparedness, and that a plan is only as good as the people who can execute it.
But when the risk is personal, those ideas take on a heavier meaning.
Receiving a Cancer Diagnosis
I was diagnosed after a routine physical that included a PSA blood test. I had not noticed any symptoms and had no known family history. That raised a few eyebrows and ultimately, a stage-three prostate cancer diagnosis.
My experience is not a case for making a personal health choice or offering clinical advice. That’s far from my wheelhouse. However, it is a helpful framework for a profession that often talks about preparedness, leadership and resilience, but sometimes forgets to consider the people expected to deliver all three.
Risk Appetite Changes When the Asset is You
In professional life, leaders can be admirably objective. They can challenge a security control, decide whether a certain risk falls within an agreed tolerance, and explain to a board why a difficult trade-off is necessary. They are typically analyzing a faceless enterprise.
Risk management is more than recommending a set of analytical frameworks. It is also decision making under duress, usually done with incomplete information and nervous tempers. Leaders who never acknowledge t…

articles.title: En Argentina, robot aprende a abrir puertas viendo videos tutoriales

Un robot capaz de abrir puertas que nunca vio antes funciona en pruebas dentro del Distrito Tecnológico de Parque Patricios, en Buenos Aires. No lo guía ningún operador humano ni tiene cargado un plano de cada acceso: aprendió observando más de mil videos de manijas, pestillos y giros.
La máquina, equipada con ruedas y un brazo de seis grados de libertad, logró en una de sus pruebas abrir una puerta metálica a los 22 centímetros de desplazamiento tras varios intentos fallidos, según informó Diario22.
Qué significa que un robot “aprenda” de videos y no de instrucciones
Un robot logra abrir puertas desconocidas entrenándose exclusivamente con grabaciones, sin planos ni control remoto previo. El sistema identifica patrones de manijas, alturas y resistencias a partir de lo observado, y aplica esas reglas a situaciones nuevas con una efectividad del 84% en las pruebas realizadas en la ciudad.
Esa cifra surgió al exponer el robot a 14 puertas inéditas en tres edificios de Retiro, Balvanera y Núñez: madera con marco viejo, chapa cortafuego, vidrio con herrajes cromados y aluminio negro. De 56 intentos, el tiempo promedio de apertura fue de 19 segundos desde el primer fotograma captado.
Las fallas se concentraron en dos escenarios puntuales: perillas redondas sin palanca, donde el mecanismo de agarre no encuentra puntos de apoyo claros, y superficies muy reflectantes, que distorsionan la lectura de las cámaras.

Un equipo del Institut d'Economia de Barcelona estuvo buscando esa grieta entre los datos de empleo de los últimos cinco años, ocupación por ocupación. El resultado permite extraer algunas conclusiones interesantes sobre el impacto de la IA en las profesiones más expuestas a ella.

Por cada diez puntos adicionales de exposición a la IA, el paro de cada profesión subió un 1,2% en los 25 meses tras el lanzamiento de ChatGPT a finales de 2022.
Más allá de ese periodo, con la IA más presente en las empresas, el porcentaje de paro por cada diez puntos de exposición se incrementa hasta el 1,7%. India’s IG Defence and Oman’s MSA Global have signed an exploratory MoU to explore co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf.
India’s IG Defence and Oman-based MSA Global have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore the co-development and local manufacture of drone and counter-drone systems for Oman and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
The agreement links India’s defence-export ambitions with Gulf security concerns, but remains exploratory and does not confirm an order, factory or deployment.

Earlier this month, the team behind Hydro developed a new way to check that a distributed system still works correctly when it resends messages after a failure.
This produced what Shadaj Laddad described to me as “like a 5000 line PR.” Hydro is an open-source Rust framework for distributed systems, the software that runs across many machines at once, and agents now write most of it with humans driving. The PR was difficult to split into smaller pieces as its components worked together.
That’s a lot of code to review for a tool developers count on to catch bugs. Laddad, research lead for the Hydro team at AWS, says it’s something the team spends a lot of time thinking about. I sat down with him last week at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose. He was set to give a keynote the next day where he was going to argue code review can’t keep pace with how agents write code.
Agents have let the team aim higher, Laddad told me, saying PRs arrive faster and run longer. “You can have the feature work well in isolation, then you mix it with something else, and suddenly the guarantees break down,” he said.
And you can’t just trust the tests. In most agent workflows, he says, the agent writes both the code and the unit tests. “Agents are great, but they’re unpredictable,” Laddad said. What we know so far: When US-China trade relations reached an all-time low last year, many global electronics manufacturers made a beeline for alternative low-cost manufacturing locations such as Thailand, Vietnam, and India. However, with skyrocketing component costs squeezing profit margins, some of these companies are reportedly shifting at least part of their PC manufacturing operations back to China.
According to Nikkei Asia, American PC giant HP and Taiwanese consumer electronics firm Asus have already moved some of their manufacturing operations back to China. Another leading PC OEM, Dell, is also said to be evaluating whether to follow suit and shift some of its PC production back to the Asian nation to offset rising component costs.
The renewed preference for China as a PC manufacturing hub underscores broader, systemic pressures gripping the global electronics supply chain. According to the report, PC makers expect that moving production back to China will allow them to leverage established infrastructure and benefit from lower input prices than those available in alternative destinations.
The resurgence of China as a hub for PC manufacturing also highlights the challenges faced by emerging low-cost destinations, both in terms of pricing power and infrastructural readiness. The move would also likely delay the much-hyped return of domestic electronics manufacturing to the US despite the announcement of several financial and other incentives.

articles.title: Google lança Gemini 4 Carbon com avanços em cibersegurança, mas você ainda não pode usá-lo • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Google lança Gemini 4 Carbon com avanços em cibersegurança, mas você ainda não pode usá-lo
Modelo supera números da Anthropic e OpenAI em testes gerais da Artificial Analysis e avança em capacidades de segurança.
Apenas duas semanas após o anúncio do Gemini 4 Argon, o Google já lançou o que considera o seu novo modelo de fronteira. O Gemini 4 Carbon é destinado a tarefas avançadas de programação e cibersegurança, incluindo identificação de vulnerabilidades em ambientes controlados e correção de códigos.
O modelo, apresentado nesta quarta-feira (29/10), não chega ao público geral por enquanto. Como tem sido comum desde o Claude Mythos 5 para modelos com tamanho poder, o Carbon será inicialmente restrito a especialistas de defesa digital enquanto conduz avaliações de segurança com autoridades dos Estados Unidos.
O Google prevê liberar os primeiros acessos por API entre daqui a uma e duas semanas, enquanto ainda não há prazo para a chegada ao aplicativo Gemini ou à interface para navegadores. O preço da API deve seguir a mesma tabela do modelo Argon: US$ 2 (cerca de R$ 10) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 10 (R$ 53) por milhão de tokens de saída.
O Google destaca o avanço da IA em benchmarks. No índice da consultoria independente Artificial Analysis, que mede o desempenho próximo do uso real da IA, o Gemini 4 Carbon alcançou 59 pontos. articles.title: Test de Tom The Postgirl, un jeu aux allures de conte aussi mignon qu'absurde
articles.summary:
En cette période excitante d’Halloween, l’envie de regarder des films d’horreur (y compris en famille), de lire des romans d’épouvante ou de jouer à des jeux qui font peur est plus forte qu’habituellement. Depuis le changement d’heure, le soleil se couche plus tôt, et l’ambiance est de plus en plus propice à expérimenter des œuvres plus noires que d’habitude
Mais attention, il n’y a pas besoin pour autant de lancer Silent Hill 2 pour se retrouver plongé dans un univers étrange, ou d’aller jouer à Hellraiser: Revival pour ressentir quelque chose de viscéral. C’est justement la proposition de Tom the Postgirl, jeu aussi étrange que loufoque, qui ressemble à un épisode de Twin Peaks qui aurait croisé le chemin d’un livre pour enfants bizarre. Tom the Postgirl sort ce jeudi 29 octobre sur PC et Mac via Steam, ainsi que sur Nintendo Switch. Il est vendu 9,99 €. Le jeu est l’œuvre du petit studio suisse Oopsie Daisies, qui le coproduit avec Arte France. Voici notre test, sans divulgâchage, du jeu le plus déroutant de ce mois d’octobre.
Points forts
- Un humour noir qui fait mouche

Points faibles

articles.title: ‘Shaking from head to toe’ — How the facial recognition blame game leaves shoppers stranded
articles.summary:
‘Shaking from head to toe’ — How the facial recognition blame game leaves shoppers stranded
Inside the ‘Kafkaesque nightmare’ of clearing your name
Mary could tell that her husband was “distraught” the moment he was wrongly accused of shoplifting and ordered to leave Home Bargains. The ordeal left him feeling “isolated”. “I was scared to go into a shop,” he said. They had only popped out to pick up some vitamins.
Elsewhere, a woman’s husband was left “shaking from head to toe” after she was told to leave Budgens on account of stealing “loads of meat” the week before. “My mind was racing,” she said. They hadn’t been to that shop for months.
Facial recognition is an inherently personal and intimate technology. It scans your features, processes your biometric data and, depending on its results, can stop you from entering a particular space.
It might all happen in an instant but its impact extends far and can be surprisingly long lasting — something that is made all the worse by a dizzying lack of clarity about who is to blame when something goes wrong.
‘Taste the indifference’
Earlier this week, in a cramped room in the House of Commons, people wrongly accused of shoplifting by facial recognition technology met to discuss their experiences with Labour MP for Stoke-on-Trent South, Dr Allison Gardner.
The event, sponsored by the civil liberties group Big Brother Watch, was designed to give people an opportunity to air their grievances with politicians, the media, and the companies…

A BCA é uma coalizão de organizações que desenvolvem navegadores que defende, principalmente, o direito dos usuários de Windows de escolherem livremente um browser para usar. Fazem parte da aliança empresas como Google, Vivaldi, Opera, Midori, Wavebox e BrowserWorks.

Our first step at defining a CPU benchmark for agentic AI — how we can measure throughput of agentic AI workloads without any GPU involved
The future of agentic AI lies in CPUs, or so the story goes. Here’s our first attempt to measure that.
Agentic AI has set off a firestorm in the world of CPUs over the past six months, yet it’s an area of performance that still doesn’t have solid, repeatable benchmarks to evaluate where the latest hardware falls. We’ve been working on an internal set of tests to evaluate at least one aspect of contentious agentic loops end-to-end, isolating CPU and memory performance from the accelerator to understand how these components contribute to the agentic loop.
This is still a work in progress, but we wanted to bring Tom’s Hardware Premium readers behind the scenes to understand how we’re going about tackling this problem, our methodology for testing, and detail what we’ve learned about agentic loops along the way. We've prototyped the test and settled the central design, but there's still work to do before the numbers it produces hold up to scrutiny.
Given that this area of computing is bleeding-edge and rapidly evolving, we undoubtedly have blind spots here. That’s OK. articles.title: Ransomware on a Home PC vs a Work Laptop: Same Click, Very Different Consequences - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Understanding the Threat Landscape
Ransomware attacks have become one of the most widespread cybersecurity threats globally, targeting both individuals and organizations. While many users may view ransomware as a personal issue affecting only individual devices, the reality is far more complex. The consequences of a ransomware attack on a home PC can be severe, but when the same attack hits a work laptop, the stakes rise dramatically, impacting not just the user but entire organizations and their stakeholders.
Ransomware typically involves malicious software encrypting files on a device, making them inaccessible until a ransom is paid. However, the impact varies greatly depending on the environment. The difference between a home PC and a work laptop is not only ownership but also the scope and scale of the damage that can follow. Understanding these distinctions is critical for effective prevention and response strategies.
The Home PC Scenario: Personal Data at Risk
When ransomware strikes a home PC, the primary victims are the individual user and their personal data. Photos, documents, and other files can be locked away, causing frustration and potential loss of irreplaceable memories or essential information. The financial impact is often limited to the ransom demand and possible costs for recovery software or professional help, but the emotional and practical toll can be significant.
Many home users rely on their computers for online banking, tax filing, managing sensitive…

articles.title: How Edge AI Helps Humanoid Robots React Faster Than a Central GPU - EE Times
articles.summary:
STMicroelectronics argued that humanoid robots should use onboard sensors and cameras to handle fast reactions on the robot, and leave only whole-body coordination to a central GPU, because a round trip to the GPU adds latency a moving robot cannot afford. The chipmaker is still weighing whether to build more powerful MCUs or MPUs for the task, a decision it says depends on how the robotics market develops.
“Every millisecond counts,” Allan Lagasca, director of STMicroelectronics’ robotics segment strategic program, told EE Times. “If you want a fast reaction, you should move the processing to the edge. If you want the entire system to work together, that is where the GPU comes in.”
Running inference closer to the task can reduce the workload sent to a central GPU and avoid delays associated with transferring data and returning commands, Lagasca said. In robotics, those delays can affect physical movement.
When two hands coordinate to transfer an object, for example, a delayed command can cause a joint to miss its target. Even if individual joints miss their targets by only a few millimeters, the combined movement can be affected.
“If inference is performed at the edge, the system can send the necessary command locally and respond faster,” he said.

articles.title: Winzig, aber heikel: Nasa-Rover Perseverance entdeckt ultrafeine Staubpartikel auf dem Mars
articles.summary:
Gefahr für Astronauten? Nasa-Rover Perseverance entdeckt ultrafeine Staubpartikel auf dem Mars
Über 1645 Marstage hinweg hat der Nasa-Rover Perseverance feine und ultrafeine Marsstaubpartikel gemessen, die sich auf mitgeführten Proben von Raumanzugmaterialien abgesetzt hatten. Einige dieser Partikel sind theoretisch klein genug, um tief in die Lunge vorzudringen und womöglich sogar in den Blutkreislauf überzugehen. Jetzt wurden die Ergebnisse in den Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences veröffentlicht.
Feine und ultrafeine Partikel
Frühere Messungen erfassten Marsstaubpartikel mit einem Durchmesser von bis zu etwa 3 Mikrometern. Das „Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry“ (PIXL) an Bord von Perseverance wies jetzt zwei noch kleinere Partikelklassen nach: feine Partikel mit einer Größe von 2,5 Mikrometern und ultrafeine, etwa 100 Nanometer große – oder wohl eher kleine – Partikel. Zum Vergleich: Die ultrafeinen Partikel sind rund 700-mal dünner als ein menschliches Haar. Die PIXL-Ergebnisse sind die ersten Vor-Ort-Messungen von feinen und ultrafeinen Partikeln auf dem Mars.
Welcher Stoff hält den Marsstaub besser ab?
Die winzigen Partikel könnten tief in die Lunge von Astronaut:innen vordringen, in den Blutkreislauf übertreten und unter Umständen lebenswichtige Organe beeinträchtigen. articles.title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
articles.summary:
Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock.
It wasn’t to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat.
That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side.
Back to the future?
Concentrated solar, also called solar thermal, is pretty simple in principle. Most of the site is covered with heliostats, devices that incorporate mirrors and a motorized tracking system that can keep their focus on a single point as the Sun moves across the sky. articles.title: Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw — security updates neglected in a series of catastrophic errors
articles.summary:
Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw — security updates neglected in a series of catastrophic errors
In their defense, Synology's misleading update policies didn't help.
Systems administrators are among the first to point out lax security policies in other companies' or people's setups. Sometimes, they are the ones who get bitten by not taking the same advice they will so readily dispense. Such is the tale of Reddit user NakamuraHwang, who had files on their Synology DS918+ NAS encrypted by a ransomware attack after making a series of unforced errors.
Hwang appears to be quite technically proficient and provided a detailed write-up of the situation. The key points, however, are that the unit in question (a) had its web interface exposed to the internet and (b) was roughly 18 months out-of-date with security patches. Just like the recent PHP snafu has adeptly shown, complacency is a far worse enemy than an army of AI bots.
The tech has a 3-2-1 backup setup, so they seemingly didn't lose any data. They attached the disks to a Proxmox machine for further inspection — Synology's DSM operating system uses mdraid underneath, so you can take the disks to another box and mount them there. articles.title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays

The AI agent associates the test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on consensus from up to three LLMs and evaluations from vision models.
At one end of the spectrum, legacy approaches to web application testing, while largely automated, do not incorporate AI as a key productivity factor. At the other extremity, innovative teams follow a fully agent-based automated approach to testing where the agent is front and center, handling every browser interaction dynamically.
The legacy approaches often falls prey to known pain points. Test suites commonly depend on implementation details (CSS classes, attributes, data-testid) that may change even when the specifications remain constant, causing unnecessary test rewriting and refactoring. Flaky tests result from the inherently inpredictible nature of the complex, asynchronous and distributed systems underlying web applications (race conditions, latency, dropped calls).

articles.title: Sam Altman almost scrapped token pricing. Here’s why he backed off.
articles.summary:
Sam Altman almost scrapped token pricing. Here’s why he backed off.
OpenAI considered dropping token-based pricing for its next model, letting developers submit a prompt and receive a price for the work, before negative customer feedback convinced the company to back away from the idea, CEO Sam Altman says.
The flat-fee pricing idea
Speaking Thursday with Stripe President John Collison on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman recalls that OpenAI “almost made a very — what would’ve been a bad call” to stop pricing its next model in tokens altogether, moving instead to an arrangement where a developer hands over a prompt and OpenAI hands back a price.
The billing would have worked “like AWS,” he explained, where you “just do something and we send you a bill” rather than metering the exchange token by token. Altman does not name the model in question or give a timeline for when the change was under consideration.
We’ve cued up the exchange in the video below:
Why customers pushed back
The idea ran into resistance when OpenAI tried to gauge how customers felt about receiving a price with no breakdown. “The customer response on that is so negative,” Altman recounts, with buyers telling the company, “’I need to know what I’m paying for somehow.’”
“’I need to know what I’m paying for somehow.’”

articles.title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
articles.summary:
Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks.
Traditional OAuth bearer tokens operate on a "finders-keepers" model, making them vulnerable to Infostealer malware (e.g. RedLine, NodeStealer) and Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks.
To prevent this types of attacks, DPoP uses cryptography to bind tokens to an asymmetric key pair generated by the client. Consequently, a stolen token cannot be replayed without the corresponding private key, which remains under the client’s control.
Google OAuth platform supports DPoP only for refresh tokens, while access tokens, which are shorter-lived, remain standard Bearer tokens. This decision is motivated by the fact that long-lived refresh tokens are "the primary vector for persistent online impersonation", whereas applying DPoP to access tokens would introduce "asymmetric cryptographic verification overhead" for each request.
It is worth noting that adopting DPoP adds several client-side requirements, including generating cryptographic keys, handling timestamps and nonces correctly, generating the appropriate HTTP headers and the required DPoP proof JWTs.
While DPoP provides protection for API tokens, it does not protect standard web application session cookies, which remain vulnerable to Infostealer malware. To address the threat of cookie theft, Google and the Web Incubator Community Group (WICG)…

articles.title: Hugging Face malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
articles.summary:
A cryptomining and backdoor campaign that abuses Hugging Face model repositories came back within days of being taken down.
Its most popular malicious model was downloaded more than 28,000 times.
Separately, researchers flagged a fake Solana starter kit on GitHub, live since late 2025, that is positioned to trick AI coding agents into installing a remote access trojan.
Code runs before the model loads
Researchers at Pluto Security found 31 malicious repositories across seven Hugging Face accounts, published in two waves since September.
The models pose as small Qwen2 test checkpoints. They target GPU hosts running self-hosted inference servers such as Xinference and GPUStack.
With linked models included, the repositories have more than 32,000 downloads. Pluto notes that this counts downloads, not confirmed infections.
Instead of using poisoned weights or pickle exploits, the campaign abuses a Hugging Face option, trust_remote_code, that lets a model ship its own Python code. When a user enables it, that code runs on their machine as soon as the model loads.
The most downloaded model, MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny, contained no actual model at all. Its code quietly installs a cryptocurrency miner disguised as a Linux system process, restarts it if killed, and removes competing miners from the machine.
Some versions also open a reverse shell, giving the attacker direct access to the infected server.

articles.title: Smarter Power Sequencing with GreenPAK™ - EE Times
articles.summary:
Programmable mixed-signal devices can replace sprawling RC networks and firmware-dependent control with compact, deterministic, and adaptable multi-rail sequencing.
Modern processors, FPGAs, memory modules, sensors, and high-speed interfaces rarely operate from a single supply. Each device may require several voltage rails, and those rails often must rise and fall in a defined order. A core supply may need to stabilize before an I/O rail; a memory rail may need to follow a processor rail; and a reset signal may not be released until every relevant voltage is valid. If that choreography is wrong, the result can be excessive inrush current, back-powering, latch-up, corrupted initialization, or, in some cases, device damage.
Why traditional sequencing becomes difficult
The simplest sequencer uses RC delays and logic gates to shift regulator-enable signals. That approach can be adequate for a small, fixed design, but it becomes unwieldy as rail count and supervision requirements grow. Every added stage introduces more passives, more tolerance stack-up, and more potential failure points. Capacitor and resistor variation, temperature, leakage, and aging can shift the effective delay. A timing change late in development may require component substitutions, schematic edits, new layout work, and another board spin.
A microcontroller offers more flexibility, but it also introduces software into a function that may be required before the main processor is ready. Firmware has to boot, ex…

The campaign exploits gamers' willingness to experiment with unofficial software, making malicious downloads look like a normal part of the process. It highlights how familiar project names can earn users' trust before they verify who is behind the files.
A cleanup script deletes the malware's own files, making the intrusion harder for the PC's owner to detect. The bureau began probing Rogers over those plans back in 2023, raising issues with how the company positioned the plans as having unlimited data when the plans also apply speed reductions — known as throttling — after a certain amount of use.
“Today, the Competition Tribunal released its decision in the Bureau’s case against Rogers and ordered the company to pay a $15 million penalty in connection with the marketing of its Infinite wireless plans,” said Jeanne Pratt, Interim Commissioner of Competition, in a statement.
“The Bureau alleged that Rogers engaged in deceptive marketing by advertising its Infinite wireless plans as offering unlimited data despite a significant reduction in speed after using a set amount.”
Along with the fine, the Tribunal ordered Rogers to publish a corrective notice and pay the Bureau’s legal costs. The full reasoning behind the Tribunal’s decision is expected to be released within 10 business days.

Lembra do Cloud Rebuild? Trata-se de um modo de restauração do Windows 11 que funciona a partir das nuvens, dispensando o usuário de ter que usar um pendrive ou uma partição dedicada para esse fim. Mas isso só funciona quando os mesmos drivers podem ser instalados via Windows Update.
Na prática, o Cloud Rebuild permite fazer uma instalação nova e completa do Windows 11, evitando, por exemplo, que você se depare com um componente (como as saídas de áudio ou uma porta Ethernet) que não funciona após o procedimento ser realizado.
