Pour le concevoir, des fournisseurs comme AMI, Insyde et Phoenix s'appuient sur EDK II, une base de code open source reprise dans les firmwares de serveurs du monde entier. Des chercheurs d'Anthropic et de Google y ont décelé une erreur de gestion de la mémoire vieille de 16 ans, que TianoCore, la communauté responsable du projet, a rendue publique la semaine dernière. Le correctif a déjà été intégré au code source d'EDK II, mais sa distribution s'annonce autrement plus compliquée que sa mise au point.

Apple’s Mac computers are known for being on the pricey side, and the ongoing memory and component shortage caused by AI data centres and other issues hasn’t helped. Still, the company’s new maxed-out Mac Studio spec is… well, it costs as much as a new car.

- In Canada, the Mac Studio M5 Ultra starts at $7,799.
- The 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU is $1,950, bringing your total to $9,749.
- Now this is the big money. If you want 512GB of RAM, it’s $23,250, bringing your total to $32,999.
- 16TB of storage costs $11,250, bringing your total to $44,249.
- And if you want to add some software like Final Cut Pro pre-installed, it’s $399.99, and Logic Pro pre-installed costs $249.99.
- Bringing your total to $44,898.98 or $2,030.20/mo for 24 months at 7.99 per cent APR.
While fun to point at the big, crazy number and have a laugh, this isn’t a purchase most people will make.
A fully loaded Mac like this might make sense for high-level video work, 3D modelling, locally run AI workloads, and other stuff that requires huge amounts of memory.

articles.title: Underwater data centers are heading for waters that endangered whales call home
articles.summary:
In context: Pilot projects have demonstrated that undersea data centers can operate reliably without significant heat-dissipation issues. However, underwater environments support fragile ecosystems that could be seriously disrupted by artificial computing infrastructure.
Earlier this year, DeepGreen Holdings filed a preliminary permit application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The company is seeking to develop two data center projects designed to take advantage of underwater environments, but the proposed locations overlap with habitats of two endangered whale populations. Local communities have also voiced strong opposition to the projects.
DeepGreen plans to build its facilities beneath Cook Inlet, in Alaska, and in the Gulf of Maine. The proposed Cook Inlet facility would consist of 66 modular data center "pods," powered by 330 to 350 tidal turbines. The company expects the installation to generate 100 megawatts of power, most of which would be used to run the underwater data center.
The Maine project would be smaller, with 50 tidal turbines providing 51 megawatts of power to a cluster of data center pods. Both projects could affect the habitats of two distinct endangered whale populations. Cook Inlet is home to a genetically isolated population of beluga whales, while the Gulf of Maine serves as a feeding ground for North Atlantic right whales.

Microsoft confirmó que este comportamiento responde al diseño actual de Windows Update y no a un error de programación. articles.title: The AI buildout's carbon bill could undo 15 years of power sector emissions cuts

In a nutshell: Data centers have already drawn widespread resistance over their impact on electricity prices and water supplies, and estimates of how their energy use might affect carbon emissions have recently grown. Still, projections vary widely, owing to uncertainty over renewables and over how many data centers will actually be built in the next several years.
In a report obtained by Bloomberg, the environmental nonprofit Sierra Club estimates that planned US AI data centers would add 618 million metric tons to the power sector's carbon emissions between 2025 and 2030, a 42% increase. The figure would effectively reverse 15 years of greenhouse gas reductions from electricity generation.
Adding that much CO2 would bring the sector's 2030 emissions to 2.1 billion metric tons. The latest estimate of the AI buildout's effect is between two and four times what the group would have projected a year and a half ago.
Many of these data centers are turning to new power sources of their own to avoid waiting to plug into existing grids. While that might ease the strain on residential grids and electricity prices, these off-grid sources could add more than 460 million metric tons of emissions, roughly equal to Mexico's annual emissions.

articles.title: Hay quien dice que crujirse los nudillos provoca artritis. Un médico pasó 50 años haciéndolo para demostrar qué hay de cierto
articles.summary:
Es bastante común que, cuando una persona comienza a crujirse los nudillos, aparezca alguien que apunte a que hacer eso es malísimo para los huesos, puesto que puede acelerar la aparición de artritis. Pero esta típica frase de madre o abuelo tiene bastante de mito detrás, como demostró un médico que estuvo crujiéndose los nudillos durante muchos años para ver el efecto que tenía.
Un médico alergólogo llamado Donald L. Unger estaba harto de escuchar estas advertencias durante su infancia y es por ello que optó por convertir su cuerpo en un laboratorio a largo plazo. Para ello, durante décadas Unger se crujió religiosamente los nudillos de su mano izquierda al menos dos veces al día, dejando la mano derecha completamente intacta como control.
Una vez hecho esto, fue en 1998, tras 50 años de experimento, cuando publicó una carta al editor en la revista Arthritis & Rheumatism. Su conclusión aquí fue rotunda, puesto que, tras comparar ambas manos, no había rastro de artritis en ninguna de las dos y no existían diferencias radiográficas entre ellas.
Los grandes estudios. Más allá de este caso que puede ser tan cómico, hay otros grandes estudios que buscan entender si una práctica que es tan habitual puede ser tan perjudicial para nuestra salud. Por ejemplo, en el año 1975, un estudio analizó a pacientes geriátricos y no encontró ninguna correlación entre el hábito de crujirse los dedos y los cambios degenerativos en las articulaciones.

El recurso de una voz conocida ya no alcanza para confirmar una identidad. Según ESET, la inteligencia artificial facilitó la imitación de voces y elevó la capacidad de persuasión de estas maniobras. Qué pasa si solicitan dinero con urgencia
El primer elemento suele ser la presión. Quien llama afirma que necesita dinero de inmediato por un accidente, una detención, un inconveniente durante un viaje o un supuesto bloqueo de una cuenta. El objetivo es reducir el tiempo disponible para evaluar la situación y llevar a que la persona actúe bajo miedo o preocupación.
Expertos aseguran que la solicitud puede incluir frases como “no cortes”, “no avises a nadie” o “hay que resolverlo ahora”. La falta de tiempo es parte del mecanismo de la estafa, porque evita que el destinatario consulte a un familiar, contacte al banco o confirme el episodio por una vía independiente.

Sus creadores consideran que, tras nuevas etapas de desarrollo y pruebas de seguridad, podría utilizarse para atender casos de sangrado gastrointestinal, enfermedad inflamatoria intestinal, obstrucciones, lesiones y tumores ubicados en el intestino delgado.
Este órgano mide cerca de 6 metros, tiene un diámetro aproximado de 2,5 centímetros y se encuentra plegado en una zona profunda del abdomen. Esa combinación dificulta que los médicos alcancen áreas donde pueden aparecer hemorragias, pólipos u otras alteraciones que requieren diagnóstico o intervención.
El procedimiento actual exige entrenamiento y puede prolongarse durante horas
En la actualidad, una de las principales alternativas para examinar el intestino delgado es la enteroscopia de doble balón. Companhia critica métricas baseadas em tokens e linhas de código para medir produtividade.
A Amazon está revendo como avalia o uso de inteligência artificial por seus engenheiros de software. Em uma nova orientação interna, a empresa afirma que quantidade de tokens consumidos, adoção de ferramentas e volume de alterações em código são métricas “profundamente falhas” quando usadas como metas.
A companhia não está abandonando a IA. A mudança é de foco: em vez de premiar quem usa mais ferramentas ou gera mais código, a Amazon quer avaliar o impacto do trabalho sobre clientes, negócios e equipes.
Um dos problemas é o chamado “tokenmaxxing”, expressão usada para descrever o consumo exagerado de tokens para elevar indicadores internos. Tokens são as unidades usadas pelos modelos para processar e gerar informações e também influenciam o custo de operação dessas ferramentas.
Segundo a Fortune, a Amazon alerta que transformar esse consumo em objetivo pode aumentar despesas sem necessariamente melhorar os resultados. O problema não é apenas teórico. Funcionários da companhia chegaram a executar agentes de IA em tarefas desnecessárias só para elevar seus números em um ranking interno descontinuado em maio.
Para o vice-presidente da Amazon, Terk Terkowitz, o melhor critério são os resultados obtidos no longo prazo. Isso inclui impacto para clientes, para o negócio e para as próprias equipes. Indicadores como consumo de tokens e adoç…

Por si fuera poco la sola estampa, basta mirar atrás para medir el contraste: en febrero, tras duplicar sus reservas en solo tres semanas, el embalse rozaba el 89 % de su capacidad, unos 68 hectómetros cúbicos. Ocho meses después, hay fines de semana en que los visitantes llegan en autobús para caminar entre el barro y las ruinas.
El pueblo ya se había mudado. Lo que emerge no es, sin embargo, el origen de Mansilla. Desde 2016, un equipo de arqueólogos excava junto a la ermita de Santa Catalina, el único edificio que quedó en pie en la orilla. Es solo el ábside y el presbiterio de una iglesia románica que fue la parroquia medieval del pueblo. Bajo ella han encontrado tres templos superpuestos y, debajo, un edificio tardorromano. Hay cerámica celtibérica y romana, y un incendio que el carbono 14 sitúa en la primera iglesia entre los años 576 y 654.

Between the executive briefings and keynotes, theoretical physicist, City College of New York professor, and best-selling author Michio Kaku gave a talk on the waves of innovation (Figure 1). The idea is closely associated with economist Joseph Schumpeter, whose theory of creative destruction states that new inventions render older ones obsolete.
Kaku traced these waves from steam power during the Industrial Revolution, through the transistor and the Information Age, to today’s AI revolution. As with many of Kaku’s talks, it was a thought-provoking glimpse into what the future could hold at our current pace of technological advancement.

Cybercriminals are, once again, exploiting people’s interest in AI tools to distribute cryptojackers and make money - this time around, opting for a combination of spoofed popular products, trusty old GitHub, and a little SEO poisoning.

Usually, when threat actors spoof legitimate software and try to disseminate it via GitHub, they go the extra mile to feign legitimacy - they artificially inflate download numbers, deploy bots to ramp up stars or forks numbers, and post fake comments. That way, when a victim opens the page, they have no reason to doubt they’re looking at legitimate, popular software.

Microsoft is bringing some of its Xbox console technology to Windows PCs with the introduction of DirectX Dump Files. When a GPU crashes on your PC, you can investigate what happened in the same way Xbox developers do with their GPU crashes, gaining insight into the underlying issues. With the latest Agility SDK 1.620 and PIX 2610.28, DirectX Dump Files provide data from Windows, Direct3D, and GPU drivers to help investigate a crash, understand its cause, and improve the graphics rendering pipeline to prevent future crashes. Joining Microsoft in this effort are AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm.
The process begins with a GPU crash. Once the GPU stops its graphics processing, DirectX creates a new dump file containing traces of what occurred before Windows resets the GPU. This includes the last Direct3D runtime state, hardware and driver data, and up to 2 MB of data from the game developer that might be traced. These files can be saved on developers' machines, but on players' PCs in production, they aren't saved by default. However, game developers can set up a crash pipeline to send crash data back to them for analysis. Once the data is available, Microsoft's PIX tool, used for performance-tuning and debugging DirectX 12 games, helps analyze the situation. articles.title: DirectX Raytracing Gets Clustered Geometry for Higher FPS and Up to 90% VRAM Savings
articles.summary:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
DirectX Raytracing Gets Clustered Geometry for Higher FPS and Up to 90% VRAM Savings
Microsoft has released one of the most significant updates to its DirectX Raytracing (DXR) since its debut in 2018. This update officially introduces clustered geometry and partitioned top-level acceleration structure (PTLAS). With clustered geometry, Microsoft envisions scenes where all animated and generated geometry is broken down into simple, reusable clusters of triangles. Typically, scenes repeatedly build large bottom-level acceleration structures, which incur additional compute costs. By using clustered geometry, ray tracing can utilize full detailed geometry used for standard rasterization instead of proxies, ensuring that ray-traced shadows and reflections match the currently visible scene.
In open-world games, using a top-level acceleration structure (TLAS) can lead to massive VRAM and compute demands. To address this, DXR now introduces partitioned TLAS (PTLAS), allowing ray tracing to focus on changes in a specific region while retaining acceleration-structure data elsewhere. Clustered geometry and PTLAS can be used together or separately, with no limitations. Below image is NVIDIA's sample of clustered geometry in action, visualized in three stages: default, clusters, and triangles applied.Benchmarks follow.

PSA: Fake KytyPS5 and AnyPS5 Repos on GitHub Are Spreading Malware
Fake GitHub repositories posing as two PS5 projects, the KytyPS5 emulator and the AnyPS5 porting tool, are being used to spread password-stealing malware, according to NordVPN's Threat Intelligence team. As reported by Tom's Hardware, visitors get pointed to a ZIP file whose Windows executable unpacks a hidden multi-stage loader. The loader first checks whether it's on a real gaming PC, and exits if the system has less than 2 GB of RAM or no physical GPU, or looks like a virtual machine or cloud server. It seems built to dodge sandboxes and security researchers. Here's how NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis put it:
Emulation fans are a perfect target. They are used to downloading experimental software from GitHub and running unsigned files, so nothing about this feels suspicious. But this is not an emulator. It steals your data, hides from your antivirus and erases its own tracks before you notice anything is wrong.
On a machine that passes the aforementioned checks, the malware adds Microsoft Defender exclusion rules, then decrypts and runs a packed payload that NordVPN believes is an infostealer. A cleanup script wipes the files about two minutes later. Its self-signed certificates carry fake company names and were created the same day the malware was built, so the campaign may be automated.

El director ejecutivo y cofundador, Steve Huffman, escribió en una publicación en el sitio que la decisión es “la correcta” para la plataforma y para el negocio. Reconoció además que, para alguien cuya vida estuvo definida por la internet abierta, se trata de un cambio grande.
El cambio no será inmediato. Según TechCrunch, Reddit hará pruebas en mercados seleccionados fuera de Estados Unidos durante el cuarto trimestre y todavía no tiene un calendario para extenderlo a todos sus usuarios. La empresa también admitió que el acceso a una portada sin cuenta sigue siendo importante.
Reddit aclaró que iniciar sesión no implica renunciar al anonimato ni eliminará la opción de navegar de forma anónima, mediante un modo incógnito que está siendo reconstruido. Huffman reconoció que quedan preguntas abiertas sobre dónde deben trazarse los límites entre la experiencia con cuenta y sin ella.

La prueba se realizó con un participante del estudio clínico VOICE, un programa de Neuralink orientado a restaurar la comunicación en personas que perdieron la capacidad de hablar. Durante la demostración, el usuario conversó por teléfono con su esposa; según la empresa, la pareja había iniciado su relación justamente a través de llamadas telefónicas, lo que le dio un valor particular al ensayo.
Cómo funciona la decodificación del habla imaginada
El sistema de Neuralink traduce señales neuronales vinculadas a la intención de hablar en palabras concretas. Hasta ahora, los usuarios debían presionar un botón para iniciar y detener la grabación de esa actividad cerebral destinada a la decodificación del habla.

articles.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.summary:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network.
The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October 28. Talos calls the attacks historical but does not specify when they occurred or whether any keys were sent.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-20127 and has a CVSS score of 10.0. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on these control systems. On a Controller, the attacker can log in as a high-privileged internal account that is not root.
When Cisco disclosed the flaw in February, Talos tracked its exploitation as UAT-8616, a cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023.
In Cisco's traditional key exchange, each SD-WAN router periodically generates an AES key for its traffic and sends it to the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart). The Controller passes the keys on to other routers. A process on the Controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys.
On a compromised Controller, a KeyDrift component called LittleFilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted. For a preset list of edge routers, it pulls out their IP addresses and a 32-byte field. Talos assesses that field as the AES-256 key material that the Controller…

An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October.
The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password.
GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw.
For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again.
The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine.
Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.

articles.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
articles.summary:
26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it.
Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the results on October 28. Most were keys for cloud and AI services, led by 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs.
Zimmermann sent the vendors with the most exposed keys a list of their credentials, but he did not contact the developers who leaked them. When he published, he had not confirmed that any of the reported credentials had been revoked. So anyone who has pushed a key to a public Gitee repository cannot assume it has been revoked.
The scan ran for about a month, but Zimmermann did not provide the dates, so it is unclear how long ago the credentials were tested. He also did not say whether anyone else had used them.
He ran two secret scanners, TruffleHog and Kingfisher, over every repository. Both tried each credential against the service that issued it and kept only those that worked, he wrote.
The scanners read each repository's full commit history. A key that a developer later removed from the code could still be found and counted there.
The 26,400 figure counts each credential once, regardless of how many repositories it appeared in. By commit date, 12,242 of the credentials came from 2025, nearly half the total. Some dated to the late 2000s.

articles.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
articles.summary:
A flaw in Telegram for Android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of a victim's phone through a voice call, once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec.
The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account. Telegram fixed the flaw in version 12.10.4 of the app, released in late September, and NebuSec disclosed it on October 29.
Combined with an information-leak bug, the flaw gives the attacker an escape from the Telegram app to Android, NebuSec co-founder and chief executive Eten Zou told The Hacker News. Adding an Android root exploit then gives full control of the phone, including its messages, microphone and camera.
The flaw can be triggered in every version from 8.6.2 through 12.10.3, Zou said. Those versions came out between March 2022 and September 2026.
The company confirmed it in private voice calls on ARM64-based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects Telegram's iOS and desktop apps or group calls.
Anyone using Telegram for Android should make sure the app is on version 12.10.4 or later. The version number appears at the bottom of the app's Settings page. The flaw had no CVE identifier as of October 29.
The attack needs the victim to be called and to answer, Zou said, so setting Telegram's call privacy option to "Nobody" blocks it, and so does declining the call.
NebuSec has not seen the flaw used in real attacks, and believes no one else had realized it could be turned into remote code execution.

articles.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
articles.summary:
A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener.
As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8.
The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free.
The kernel fix credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge with reporting the bug. Neither the CVE record nor the fix mentions multipath TCP (MPTCP). The link between that feature and this bug comes from Anthropic's post.
MPTCP lets one connection use several network paths at once. On Linux, an application must request MPTCP when it opens a socket.
Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for some of their kernels, but Ubuntu and RHEL have not.

North Korea's most notorious hacking group has been caught protecting its malware with the same post-quantum cryptography that governments and tech firms are still rolling out to safeguard their own data.
In its analysis of a campaign dubbed Operation FlashHole, Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) says an updated version of LPEClient, a Lazarus Group tool, now uses ML-KEM-1024, a key exchange mechanism designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers, to secure the channel it uses to download more malware.
The findings describe a campaign active since at least July 2025 that has hit at least three South Korean organizations in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors.

Reddit deviendra une expérience « principalement connectée », a prévenu son P.-D.G, Steve Huffman, dans un message posté sur la plateforme hier, jour de la présentation des résultats trimestriels de l’entreprise. L’entreprise veut freiner les robots d’IA qui aspirent ses discussions, mais elle perd aussi chaque semaine des visiteurs venus de Google, et tire la majeure partie de ses revenus de ses membres connectés.
Six visiteurs quotidiens sur dix lisent Reddit sans compte
Au deuxième trimestre, 77,7 millions des 130,3 millions de visiteurs quotidiens de Reddit naviguaient sans être connectés, d’après les chiffres transmis par l’entreprise au gendarme boursier américain. Pour Steve Huffman, la « grande majorité » des accès non autorisés au site, autrement dit l’aspiration et le vol de ses données, passe par cette navigation anonyme. Reddit a coupé l’accès sans compte à Old Reddit, son ancienne interface, et supprimera ses flux RSS le 13 novembre, avant de fermer l’accès public à son API d’ici mars 2027. articles.title: Le chiffrement qui protège les banques en ligne pourrait céder à un ordinateur quantique plus petit que prévu
articles.summary:
La start-up française Alice & Bob estime qu’un ordinateur quantique de 22 593 qubits pourrait casser le chiffrement largement utilisé RSA-2048, en à peine trois jours. Cette estimation, quarante fois plus basse que celle de Google, concerne aussi Bitcoin.
Le chiffrement RSA-2048, qui protège la banque en ligne, les e-mails et les signatures numériques, pourrait lâcher prise face à un ordinateur quantique de seulement 23 000 qubits, contre près d'un million selon la dernière estimation de Google. C'est le record publié le jeudi 29 octobre par Alice & Bob, dans une prépublication déposée sur l'archive de l'IACR, l'association internationale de recherche en cryptologie. Avec la même recette, une clé Bitcoin tomberait en à peine une petite heure. Aucune machine de ce calibre n’existe encore, certes, mais le compte à rebours qui pèse sur la cryptographie d'Internet vient de prendre de la vitesse.
À peine 22 593 qubits pour faire tomber le chiffrement RSA
Imaginé en 1994 par le mathématicien américain Peter Shor, l'algorithme de Shor est une méthode de calcul conçue pour les ordinateurs quantiques, capable de décomposer un très grand nombre en facteurs premiers infiniment plus vite qu'une machine classique, ce qui en fait le cauchemar attitré des cryptographes. Or RSA protège une large part de notre Internet d'aujourd'hui, de la banque en ligne aux e-mails en passant par les signatures numériques. articles.title: Windows 11 : après la barre des tâches, Microsoft s'attaque enfin au clic droit
articles.summary:
Il aura fallu cinq ans pour que Microsoft s'attaque à l'un des éléments les plus controversés de Windows 11. Le menu contextuel devient personnalisable, et vous allez enfin pouvoir décider des commandes qui s'affichent lorsque vous faites un clic droit.
Après avoir rendu à la barre des tâches la possibilité de changer de place, Microsoft poursuit son entreprise de réconciliation avec les utilisateurs et utilisatrices de Windows 11. Cette fois, c'est au tour du menu contextuel, censé simplifier celui de Windows 10, mais qui a fini par imposer des manipulations supplémentaires pour accéder à certaines commandes. En juin dernier, l'éditeur avait promis de revoir sa copie, sans préciser jusqu'où irait la personnalisation ni quand elle serait disponible. Quatre mois plus tard, la mise à jour facultative KB5127936, publiée le 28 octobre pour Windows 11 25H2 et 26H2, commence à concrétiser ces engagements.
Un clic droit que vous pourrez enfin organiser à votre guise
Si vous effectuez un clic droit sur un fichier ou un dossier dans l'Explorateur, vous devriez désormais découvrir une nouvelle entrée « Personnaliser le menu », qui donne accès à une page de réglages dédiée. Vous pourrez y choisir les commandes à afficher ou à masquer, comme « Envoyer vers », « Imprimer », « Créer un raccourci » ou « Copier en tant que chemin d'accès ».
